question.problem: A traditional festival is usually held on a single day after the $6$th and before the $15$th of September. The exact day is selected each year and depends on the weather conditions. Assuming that each day after the $6$th and before the $15$th of September has the same probability of being chosen, what is the standard deviation of the selected days? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the date of the selected day. From the problem statement, we know that $X∼U\{7,8,…,14\},$ and we wish to compute $\text{SD}[X].$

In general, if $X∼U\{a,a+1,…,b\},$ then the variance of $X$ is

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\frac{|S{|}^{2}-1}{12}
$$

where $S=\{a,a+1,…,b\}.$

Now, we know that

$$
\begin{aligned}|S| & =b-a+1 \\  & =14-7+1 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for our random variable $X∼U\{7,8,…,14\},$ we have the following variance:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\frac{{8}^{2}-1}{12}=\frac{63}{12}
$$

Finally,

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\frac{63}{12}}≈2.29.
$$
